title: URL Shortener System Design: A bit.ly-Style Case Study
summary: End-to-end design of a bit.ly-style URL shortener (about 40 writes/s, 4,000 redirects/s average): requirements and estimates, API, short-code generation, storage, cached redirect path, analytics, aliases and expiry, abuse control, and scaling and failure handling.

chapters.title: URL Shortener System Design (URL Shortener)
points: Case study: design a bit.ly-style service, long URL in, 7-character short link out
Subsystems covered: API, code generation, storage, redirect and cache, analytics, aliases and expiry, rate limiting
Scale target: 100M new URLs/month, 100:1 read to write, 6B links in 5 years
Closes with failure handling, trade-offs and interview questions

chapters.title: Problem, Requirements and Scale Estimates (URL Shortener)
points: Functional: shorten a URL, redirect, custom alias, expiry, click analytics, delete a link
Non-functional: redirect p99 under 50 ms, 99.99% availability, codes unpredictable and never reused
Write estimate: 100M/month is about 40 writes/s average, about 120/s peak
Read estimate: 100:1 ratio gives about 4,000 redirects/s average, about 12,000/s at 3x peak
Storage estimate: 6B links x 500 B is about 3 TB over 5 years; metadata fits a sharded store
Cache sizing: 20% hot links, 4,000/s x 86,400 s x 20% x 500 B is about 35 GB, fits one Redis cluster
Code space: base62 with 7 chars is 62^7, about 3.5 trillion, far above 6B
Out of scope: link-in-bio pages, QR codes, A/B redirect targets

chapters.title: High-Level Architecture (URL Shortener)
points: Write path: client, API gateway, shorten service, code generator, DB, then cache warm
Read path: client, CDN or edge, redirect service, Redis, DB on miss, then 301 or 302
Redirect service is separate from the shorten service because reads are 100x writes and scale independently
Click events go async to Kafka, never on the redirect critical path
Components: LB, stateless app tier, Redis, sharded KV store, Kafka, analytics store
301 (permanent, browser caches, loses click counts) vs 302 (temporary, every click hits us)

chapters.title: API Design (URL Shortener)
points: Responsibilities: create, resolve, inspect and delete links with auth and idempotency
POST /v1/links {long_url, alias?, expires_at?} returns 201 {short_url, code}
GET /{code} returns 302 with a Location header, or 404/410 when missing or expired
DELETE /v1/links/{code} and GET /v1/links/{code}/stats require an API key
Idempotency-Key header makes retried POSTs return the same code
Errors: 400 bad URL, 409 alias taken, 429 rate limited, 410 expired
Metrics: create p99 under 200 ms, redirect p99 under 50 ms, 4xx and 5xx rates per endpoint

chapters.title: Short-Code Generation: base62, Counters, Hashing (URL Shortener)
points: base62 uses 0-9, a-z, A-Z: 7 chars is about 3.5T codes, 6 chars is about 56B
Counter plus base62: monotonic ID, encoded; no collisions but codes are guessable
Hash approach: MD5 or SHA of the URL, take the first 7 base62 chars; collisions need a check and retry
Range allocation: each app server leases 1,000 IDs from ZooKeeper or a DB, so there is no per-request coordination
Snowflake-style 64-bit IDs avoid a central counter but give longer codes (11 chars)
Anti-guessing: permute the counter with a bijective shuffle or XOR key so codes are not sequential
Mistake: truncating a hash without a collision check, or hashing the same URL to the same code when per-user links are needed

chapters.title: Data Model and Storage (URL Shortener)
points: links table: code PK, long_url, user_id, created_at, expires_at, is_active
~500 B per row; 3 TB at 5 years means shard by hash(code), 16 shards x about 200 GB
Access pattern is pure key lookup, so use a KV store (DynamoDB, Cassandra) over joins
SQL vs NoSQL: SQL gives transactions and unique constraints; NoSQL gives easy horizontal scale
Secondary index on user_id for 'my links' lists; keep it out of the hot path
Replication factor 3 with quorum reads; hot partitions mitigated by the cache
Mistake: storing click counters in the links row, which causes write contention

chapters.title: Redirect Path and Caching (URL Shortener)
points: Flow: edge cache, then Redis GET code, then DB on miss, then populate cache, then 302
Cache-aside with TTL 24 h; negative cache for unknown codes (60 s) blocks scan attacks
LRU eviction; 35 GB hot set at a 95% hit rate means DB sees about 200 reads/s
CDN caches 301s for static hot links, trading click-count accuracy for latency
Cache stampede on a viral link: request coalescing or single-flight plus jittered TTL
Invalidate on delete or expiry change by cache delete, and bound staleness with TTL
Metrics: hit rate over 95%, redirect p99 under 50 ms, DB read QPS, cache memory

chapters.title: Analytics Pipeline (URL Shortener)
points: Responsibilities: count clicks and capture referrer, country, device without slowing redirects
Redirect service publishes a click event to Kafka fire-and-forget; about 4,000 events/s, about 300 B each
Stream processor (Flink) aggregates per code per minute into a column store (ClickHouse)
Raw events kept 30 days, roll-ups kept 2 years: about 100 GB/day raw storage
Delivery is at-least-once, so dedupe on event_id to keep counts consistent
Stats API reads roll-ups: GET /stats?code=&range=7d returns series in under 300 ms
Failure: Kafka down means buffer locally and drop clicks rather than fail redirects
Metrics: consumer lag under 30 s, drop rate, event loss under 0.1%

chapters.title: Custom Aliases and Expiry (URL Shortener)
points: Alias rules: 3-30 chars, [a-zA-Z0-9-], reserved words (api, admin, login) blocked
Uniqueness through the PK: conditional insert returns 409 if taken, with no check-then-insert race
Aliases share one namespace with generated codes; reserve generated space so they cannot collide
Expiry stored as expires_at; the redirect checks it on read and returns 410 Gone
Lazy deletion on read plus a background sweeper (TTL index or daily job) reclaiming rows
Cache TTL = min(24 h, time to expiry) so expired links stop resolving promptly
Mistake: recycling expired codes, which lets an old shared link point to a stranger's URL

chapters.title: Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention (URL Shortener)
points: Limit creates per API key: 100/hour free tier; anonymous by IP, 10/hour
Token bucket in Redis (INCR plus EXPIRE or Lua script) at the gateway; return 429 with Retry-After
Redirects limited per IP at about 100/s at the edge to blunt scraping and enumeration
Malware and phishing: check the target against Google Safe Browsing at create time and re-scan nightly
Block-list known bad domains; disable a flagged link in under 1 minute, with the cache purged
Block redirect loops and self-referencing shortener domains
Failure: if the limiter store is down, fail open with a local per-node cap
Metrics: 429 rate, abuse reports per day, time-to-takedown

chapters.title: Scaling, Failure Handling and Interview Questions (URL Shortener)
points: Scale-out: stateless app tier behind LB, Redis cluster by consistent hashing, DB shards by hash(code)
Multi-region: active-active reads with geo-DNS; writes route to the home region, async replicated
Failure matrix: Redis down means DB serves (about 20x load, so rate-limit); DB shard down means replica reads
ID service outage: servers keep a prefetched 1,000-ID range, about 25 s of writes at 40/s
Trade-offs: 301 vs 302, counter vs hash, SQL vs NoSQL, sync vs async analytics
Interview Q: how do you avoid collisions across servers? Answer: range leasing or a bijective counter
Interview Q: how do you handle a viral link? Answer: CDN, single-flight and replicated hot keys
Cheatsheet numbers: 40 writes/s, 4,000 reads/s, 3 TB, 35 GB cache, 7 chars base62, p99 under 50 ms
